correctness.rationale: For an out-arborescence, only the target of a newly added link changes indegree. Descendant levels shift uniformly, so exactly two trophic differences can deviate from one and their deviations sum to zero. Solving the target equation for source outside versus inside the target subtree gives the two formulas. The zero-cost count follows by enumerating same-consecutive-depth potential edges excluding the existing parent. A standalone exact Gaussian-elimination solver independently confirmed 40,322 modifications; the general result follows from the proof, not finite testing.

value.rationale: Adding a single predation link to a basal feeding hierarchy is a motivated food-web assembly operation, and classical trophic incoherence is used as a structural indicator in established ecological research. The formula gives a complete deterministic local-response calculus independent of otherwise arbitrary branching: precise depth-only acyclic costs, a sharp cycle-length feedback penalty, and an exact count of additions that maintain perfect coherence. It provides usable analytic benchmarks for networks and assembly models without claiming universal ecological stability.
